look: A derelict, tin-roofed farm stand containing a cat bed but no produce opens onto a rutted dirt road, where dusk is closing in through thick fog.
Branches reach out over the road from both sides, far enough up that they almost meet in the middle.
Behind the stand a fence sags, four strands of wire on posts leaning crookedly.
Across the road the fog obscures something tall and unlit, too square to be trees.
Across the road the fog has thinned around a tall, unlit house.
Tire tracks show in the dried mud of the shoulder.
The air smells of cold and wet earth.
A tall foyer under a water-stained ceiling. The front door is shut behind you, with a crowded coat tree beside it and an empty cat bowl on the floor.
A cloudy mirror hangs by the door.
A stroller is parked in the corner by a pile of shoes and tiny booties.
A bulletin board hangs over a small table where a smart speaker blinks blue.
A shipping box sits half-opened against the wall.
An arched doorway opens on one side, and a wide doorway on the other.
The grand staircase is a ruin, with fresh lumber stacked beside it.
The grand staircase is mended most of the way up, but the top steps are still missing, with fresh lumber stacked beside its base.
A patched grand staircase sweeps up to the floor above.

Two dining chairs are pushed back from a long table, with a high chair beside. A candy bowl and a vase of flowers stand on the sideboard, under tall windows onto an overgrown garden. Through the arched doorway you can see a crowded coat tree, and a swinging door lets through the hum of a fridge.

A big old-fashioned kitchen. A pasta pot sits on the cast-iron stove, a drying rack stands empty by the kitchen sink, and a Keurig waits with a clean mug. The fridge-freezer hums beside the trash can, a cake box sits at the end of the counter, and the pantry door is ajar. A swinging door shows a sliver of a long table each time it moves, and through the glazed back door there are steps, then tangled green.

An overgrown sunken courtyard. Ivy swallows the side of the house, and a stone wall enclosed herb garden has run wild beside a watering can. A picnic blanket is spread over a stone bench. In the middle, a stone circle holds the last of a chalk diagram. An autumn-bronzed oak tree crowds the far wing of the house. Pumpkins wait by the kitchen steps next to a cat bowl, and at the top, the back door glows warm and smells faintly of coffee.

A room for long evenings: a deep sofa with a baby blanket, two armchairs, bookshelves and a fireplace full of cold ash. One armchair has been turned to face a bare patch of wall. A stack of board books sits on the rug. A tall curiosity cabinet stands in the corner. Through the wide doorway you can see the foot of a staircase and a pile of shoes.

A cozy library with floor to ceiling shelves packed with occult tomes bound in leather, books of folklore, and a row of paperback thrillers. A circle of scorch marks is burned into the floorboards, surrounded by scattered objects including a coil of copper wire. A spirit board lies on the floorboards just outside the circle, its planchette resting on the letter S. The air feels charged, like the moment before a storm. An empty cat bed sits in the corner. The back of a heavy cabinet blocks one wall, a keyhole set into it at waist height, and behind the shelves at the far end a small window stands propped open a crack, the crown of an oak filling it.

A long hallway lined with faded family portraits that don't belong to anyone living here. A roll-top desk stands against the wall, its lid half closed on a pile of papers, and a heavy oak wardrobe looms beside it, a short crowbar lying on the floor against the skirting board. A bad smell has got into the hallway — faint by the portraits, worse by the desk. Baby clothes hang over the railing to dry. Doors lead to a bedroom and a nursery, which emits a soft hum of white noise. The main staircase leads back down to the Entryway, its patched steps solid underfoot. A cat bowl sits at the top of the main staircase.

The main bedroom: an unmade bed, a dresser with its drawers half open, and a tall mirror over the dresser that catches the light at odd angles. A bottle warmer sits on the nightstand. In the corner, an unpacked moving box labeled HALLOWEEN overflows with costumes, a “Trick-or-Treat” welcome mat and a tangle of fake spider web. A sash window by the dresser looks down over the courtyard and the crown of the old oak, and a tin of graphite powder sits open on the sill, with ivy crowding the glass outside. The panelled bedroom door stands half open on the hallway.

A small, warm room painted a soft sage green. The crib is made up neatly under a slowly turning mobile, and a painted shelf runs along the wall above it, at adult height and well out of reach of anybody small. On the changing table, a baby monitor crackles with faint, happy sounds, though the crib is empty. The nursery door, painted the same soft sage, is pushed to but not latched on the hallway.
